# requireRegExp

<link-summary>Returns the value as a regular expression, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireRegExp() — Returns the value as a regular expression, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireRegExp(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a regular expression."): RegExp;
```

Identified by its internal tag rather than by `instanceof`, so a regular expression from another frame is recognised too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                   | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                     | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a regular expression."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`RegExp` — the same value, typed as a regular expression.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                              |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a regular expression. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireRegExp(/a/); // => /a/
requireRegExp(new RegExp("a")); // => new RegExp("a")
requireRegExp("/a/"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireRegExp({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
